inputs.text: The Taoiseach is out in Limerick claiming housing tenancies have risen even after his government's March 1 rules forced landlords into six-year leases, while brushing off the spike in eviction notices and homelessness. Yet the numbers of people in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationally. This is the predictable result of heavy-handed government interference in private rental agreements, undermining property rights and family stability instead of letting personal responsibility and market signals maintain order.

output.main_topic: Housing rental rules, rising emergency accommodation, and criticism of government interference

central_relations.subject: The Taoiseach
central_relations.action: brushing off the spike in eviction notices and homelessness
central_relations.object: the spike in eviction notices and homelessness

central_relations.subject: numbers of people in emergency accommodation

output.narrative_frame: The report frames government rental rules as harmful interference and presents rising emergency accommodation as a predictable consequence.
opinions: Government interference in private rental agreements is heavy-handed and undermines property rights and family stability.
Rising emergency accommodation is a predictable result of government interference.
Personal responsibility and market signals should be allowed to maintain order.
